description: What Excel does with an array formula's range holding another formula, with two array formulas' ranges sharing a cell, and with the edits that make either. ts-xlsx wrote each shape, authored directly and produced by its own row edits, and every package was opened interactively. Separately, Excel performed the same edits over COM on a workbook of its own, reporting whether it refused each and what the sheet held after.
probe: .claude/skills/excel-gui-automation/scripts/open-verdict.ps1 per package; a one-off COM script performing each edit (Rows.Insert, Rows.Delete, Columns.Insert, Columns.Delete, Range.Copy, Range.FormulaArray, Range.Formula) and reading HasArray, CurrentArray, HasSpill and SpillingToRange

openVerdicts.legacy B1:B3, then duplicateRow(1): repair-prompt, written as B1:B4 beside B2:B5
openVerdicts.legacy B1:B3 with B2 a value, then dupli: clean, written as B1:B4 with values in B2 and B3
openVerdicts.legacy B1:B3, then insertRow(2) carrying: repair-prompt, written as B1:B4 with the formula in B2
openVerdicts.dynamic B1:B3, then insertRow(2) carryin: repair-prompt, written as dynamic B1:B4 with the formula in B2

legacy B1:B3.insert row 1, above: allowed; the array moves to B2:B4
legacy B1:B3.insert row 2 or rows 2:3, inside: refused: You can't change part of an array.
legacy B1:B3.insert column B, at its column: allowed; the array moves to C1:C3
legacy B1:B3.copy row 3 onto row 4, or insert it at r: allowed; B4 becomes a one-cell array formula of its own
legacy B1:B3.FormulaArray over B2:B4: refused: Unable to set the FormulaArray property
legacy B1:B3.Formula into B2: reported no error and changed nothing: B2 is still a member of B1:B3

legacy B1:C3.insert column B, its left edge: allowed; the array moves to C1:D3

dynamic B1 spilling over B1:B3.insert row 2: allowed; the formula becomes A1:A4*2 and spills over B1:B4
dynamic B1 spilling over B1:B3.insert row 1 copied at row 2: allowed; B1 shows #SPILL!, B2 spills over B2:B5

repairs.probe: open-verdict.ps1 -AcceptRepair -SaveRepairedTo on packages ts-xlsx wrote and then patched, each recovery saved and its sheet part read, beside the recovery log Excel wrote to %TEMP%. Excel recalculated each recovery, so a cell it emptied inside a range kept shows what the array formula computes there.
repairs.legacy B1:B3 with a plain formula in B2: log: Cell information removed. B1:B3 kept; B2 <v>4</v>, no formula
repairs.legacy B1:B3 with a bold plain formula i: log: Cell information removed. B1:B3 kept; B2 keeps its s and holds <v>4</v>, no formula
repairs.dynamic B1:B3 with a plain formula in B2: log: Cell information removed. B1:B3 kept with its cm; B2 <v>4</v>, no formula
repairs.legacy B1:B3 beside legacy B2:B4, B2 cac: log: Cell information removed. B1:B3 kept; B2 <v>4</v>, no formula
repairs.legacy B1:B3 holding in B2 the master of: log: Cell information and Shared formula removed. B1:B3 kept; B2 <v>4</v>, C2 <v>200</v>, neither a formula
repairs.legacy B1:C2 beside legacy A2:B3, A2 cac: log: Formula removed. B1:C2 kept; A2 <v>3</v>, no formula

verdict: An array formula's range, legacy or dynamic, may hold no other formula and share no cell with another array formula's range; a member cell holding a value is what the formula produced. Excel repairs a package breaking either rule by keeping the array formula first in reading order: a formula inside its range loses its formula and its value, keeping its style, a shared formula whose master that was loses its formula and keeps its value, and an array formula whose range only shares cells with it loses its formula and keeps its value. Excel refuses any edit cutting through a legacy range: an insert strictly inside it, a delete taking part of it, a row copied onto or into it. It allows an edit that moves the whole range or removes it whole. It allows the same edits through a dynamic array, whose spill it then blocks. Locked by the corpus case an-array-formula-range-holds-no-other-formula.
